gas_tank_water_heater.what: A gas fired storage water heater. It heats and stores the hot water for the whole house: a tank kept hot by a burner under it, vented up a flue.
gas_tank_water_heater.how: Cold water comes in the dip tube to the bottom. The gas control valve senses the tank cooling and opens the gas, the burner heats the tank, the draft hood and flue carry the exhaust out the roof. Hot water leaves the top. The anode rod inside corrodes instead of the tank.
checks: Age off the data plate (8 years or older is a finding)
Temperature setting: read the dial, 120 at the tap is the target
Is the unit sized right for the home: gallons on the plate against who lives here
Anode rod: service record, or what it looked like if it was pulled
Thermal expansion tank: present, holds air on a tap, mounted
Water connections and dielectrics: dry, no crust at the unions
Drain valve and base: weeping, rust streaks, water in the pan, leak from the shell
T and P relief valve and discharge line: valve good, line full size to the floor, a receptor or outside, end visible
Gas flex and sediment trap: shutoff within reach, trap below it, modern coated flex
Vent and draft: draft proves, joints tight, no rust flakes in the hood (only if it is running)
CO detector nearby, working
Burner and combustion air: screen clear, no soot, combustion air opening
Drain pan and pan line to daylight, leak sensor on an attic unit
Thermostatic mixing valve on the hot outlet, holding temper at the tap
Scale inhibitor on the water line, in date
Label the hot water shutoff (red tag)
Label the cold water shutoff (blue tag)
Label the gas shutoff (yellow tag), show the quarter turn

electric_tank_water_heater.what: An electric storage water heater. It heats and stores the hot water for the whole house with two elements in the tank, upper and lower, each on its own thermostat.
electric_tank_water_heater.how: The upper element heats the top first, then its thermostat hands off to the lower element. 240 volt feed through its own breaker. No vent, no flame. The anode rod inside corrodes instead of the tank.
checks: Age off the data plate (8 years or older is a finding)
Temperature setting: read the thermostat dial, 120 at the tap is the target
Is the unit sized right for the home: gallons on the plate against who lives here
Anode rod: service record, or what it looked like if it was pulled
Thermal expansion tank: present, holds air on a tap, mounted
Heating elements: both meter in range from the terminals, no scorched lugs, no water in the compartment
Thermostats: each calls and cuts out at the setpoint, the high limit reset is not tripping
Water connections and dielectrics: dry, no crust at the unions
Drain valve and base: weeping, rust streaks, water in the pan, leak from the shell
T and P relief valve and discharge line: valve good, line full size to the floor, a receptor or outside, end visible
Drain pan and pan line to daylight, leak sensor on an attic unit
Thermostatic mixing valve on the hot outlet, holding temper at the tap
Scale inhibitor on the water line, in date
Label the hot water shutoff (red tag)
Label the cold water shutoff (blue tag)
Surge protection on the water heater circuit

gas_tankless_water_heater.what: A gas tankless water heater. It heats water only when a tap opens, no tank. The condensing kind drains acidic condensate and vents in PVC; the non condensing kind vents hot exhaust in stainless. The deck has one card for both.
gas_tankless_water_heater.how: The flow sensor sees the tap, the fan starts, gas lights in the sealed burner, water runs through the heat exchanger and out hot. On our water the exchanger scales up in about a year without a flush through the isolation valves.
checks: The unit: model and age off the plate, and whether it has ever been descaled
Isolation and service valves: both present with ports, not seized
Inlet water filter screen: pulled, clean, refitted
Fault code on the display: read it and write it down before touching anything
Condensate line (condensing units): draining freely to a legal point, neutralized, never into a metal pan
Venting and clearances: approved vent, sealed joints, clear of windows, soffits and the dryer vent
Gas line size and shutoff: sized for the BTU on the plate, sediment trap fitted, no leaks
Drain pan under the unit with a line to daylight
Scale inhibitor on the water line, in date
Surge protection at the equipment

electric_tankless_water_heater.what: An electric tankless water heater. Heating elements in chambers, no tank, a big electrical load: it lives and dies on the electrical feed and the scale.
electric_tankless_water_heater.how: The flow sensor sees the tap and the board staggers the elements on to hit the set point. It needs several 240 volt circuits. Scale coats the elements on our water, so the isolation valves and a yearly flush matter as much as on a gas unit.
checks: The unit: model and age off the plate, and whether it has ever been descaled
Isolation and service valves: both present with ports, not seized
Inlet water filter screen: pulled, clean, refitted
Fault code on the display: read it and write it down before touching anything
Scale inhibitor on the water line, in date
Surge protection at the equipment

hybrid_water_heater.what: A heat pump water heater: a water heater and an air conditioner in one cabinet. A small heat pump on top of the tank pulls heat from the room air into the water, so it has a filter and it makes condensate.
hybrid_water_heater.how: The fan pulls room air over the evaporator and the compressor moves that heat into the tank. The elements back it up when the heat pump cannot keep up. Condensate drains from the top unit all summer.
checks: Age off the data plate (8 years or older is a finding)
Temperature setting: read the display, 120 at the tap is the target
Thermal expansion tank: present, holds air on a tap, mounted
Drain valve and base: weeping, rust streaks, water in the pan, leak from the shell
Heat pump air filter: clean and seated, or it falls back to the elements
Condensate line: draining, pan dry, no mineral trail
Water connections and dielectrics: dry, no crust at the unions
T and P relief valve and discharge line: valve good, line full size, end visible
Thermostatic mixing valve on the hot outlet, holding temper at the tap
Scale inhibitor on the water line, in date

hvac_furnace.what: A gas furnace. The blower pushes house air over a heat exchanger warmed by the burners. That metal wall is the only thing between the fire and the air the family breathes.
hvac_furnace.how: The thermostat calls, the inducer proves draft through the pressure switch, the igniter lights the burners, the flame sensor proves flame, and the blower runs once the exchanger warms. Exhaust goes out the flue, or out PVC on a condensing unit, which also makes condensate that has to drain.
checks: Gas shutoff and sediment trap: shutoff within reach, trap below it, no leak at the joints
Heat exchanger: light and mirror in every cell; a crack or a rust out stops the job and tags the unit
Flue and venting: every joint tight and rising, no corrosion, no water heater orphaned on an oversized vent
Inducer motor: a smooth whir on startup, no bearing noise
CO detector in the home, working
Condensate drain (A coil on top): trap primed, line pitched, no rust trail on the furnace
UV or coil light fitted and inside its service life
The filter is asked once, on the Every HVAC sheet: pull it, hold it up, note the size

hvac_air_handler.what: The indoor half of a split system: a blower and a coil in a cabinet, in the attic here. Filter, coil, blower, condensate, pan and float switch.
hvac_air_handler.how: The blower pulls return air over the coil, cold in cooling and warm in heat pump mode, and pushes it down the ducts. The coil pulls gallons of water out of the air every summer day; the drain pan and line carry it away, and the float switch in the emergency pan shuts the unit down before an overflow reaches the ceiling.
checks: Blower compartment: wheel clean, no caked blades, no bearing grind
Evaporator coil: clean fins, no matted dust, no ice, no dirty sock smell
TXV sensing bulb strapped tight and insulated on the suction line
Condensate drain: line draining, trap right, pan dry
Emergency pan and float switch: pan present, line to daylight, float trips the unit
Dehumidification: the house not holding damp in July
UV or coil light fitted and inside its service life
Surge protection at the equipment
The filter is asked once, on the Every HVAC sheet

hvac_condenser.what: The outdoor unit of a split system, air conditioner or heat pump: compressor, outdoor coil and fan on a pad. The capacitor is the cheapest part out there and it takes the compressor with it.
hvac_condenser.how: Refrigerant absorbs heat inside the house, the compressor pumps it out here, and the fan blows outdoor air across the coil to dump that heat. The contactor closes on the thermostat's 24 volts to start it; the capacitor gives the motors their push. A heat pump runs the same loop backwards in winter through its reversing valve and defrosts its coil now and then.
checks: Refrigerant and age off the data plate: R-22 points at replacement; gauges only if the split says charge is the question
Condenser coil: light through the fins, no cottonwood, grass or bent fins
Refrigerant lines and insulation: suction line insulated the whole way, wall penetration sealed
Pad and clearance: level, not sunk, nothing growing within 18 inches
Condenser fan motor and blade: spins free, no wobble, amps under the label
Service valves, caps and Schrader cores: caps on, cores tight, no oil at the stems
Reversing valve and defrost, heat pump only: shifts clean both ways
Capacitor and electrical: meter the can against its rating, no bulge, discharge it first
Disconnect box: no heat marks, lugs tight, whip sound
Contactor and wiring: contacts clean, pulls in solid, no chatter, no heat at the terminals
Compressor soft start fitted

hvac_package.what: A gas pack: furnace and air conditioner in one outdoor cabinet, ducted through the wall. One cabinet hides the indoor half completely, so most homeowners do not know they have a filter at all.
hvac_package.how: Everything the split system does, in one box outside. The return and supply ducts pass through the wall to the cabinet; the burners, heat exchanger, coils, blower and condensate all live inside it.
checks: Coils, indoor and outdoor: both faces clean
Blower compartment: wheel clean, no belt or bearing noise
Refrigerant and age off the plate, and whether the tonnage still fits the house
Gas section and heat exchanger: no crack, no soot, flue sound at the cabinet
Duct connection at the curb or pad: sealed, no rotted flex, no gap
Condensate: draining downhill to a legal point, not pooling on the pad
Disconnect and electrical: no heat marks, lugs tight
Compressor soft start fitted

hvac_minisplit.what: A ductless mini split: a wall head inside, an inverter unit outside, a line set between. Screens and the blower wheel are the checks; once a homeowner sees the mold on the wheel they never forget it.
hvac_minisplit.how: The outdoor inverter varies the compressor speed. The line set carries refrigerant to the head, which blows room air over its own coil. Condensate leaves the head by gravity through the wall, so the drain line's pitch is everything.
checks: Filter screens: pulled, washed and refitted; hold them up to the light
Blower wheel and coil: no black speckling, no matted coil
Condensate drain: draining, no stain or bubbled paint under the head, line pitched

kitchen_sink.what: The kitchen sink and cabinet: stops, faucet, strainers, trap, the dishwasher connection and the cabinet floor, which is a written history of every leak nobody called about.
kitchen_sink.how: Supply stops under the sink feed the faucet. Waste falls through the strainer or the disposal into the trap, then the drain. The dishwasher drains through a high loop or an air gap into the disposal or the tailpiece.
checks: Supply lines and angle stops: both stops turn by hand, lines dry and braided
Faucet, sprayer and aerator: no drip at the base, firm in the deck, sprayer holds, aerator clear
P trap and drain: dry hand on every slip joint, no corroded metal trap
Strainer nut where it joins the sink: no seep under the basket
Dishwasher air gap or high loop: present and flowing
Under sink filter or RO: cartridges in date, no weep at the head
Cabinet base: dry, no swelling or dark rings

disposal.what: The garbage disposal. A grinder under the kitchen sink on its own circuit. A hum with no spin is a jam; a leak from the body is the end of that unit.
disposal.how: The switch runs the motor, the turntable throws the food against the grind ring, and water carries it out the discharge into the trap. The dishwasher drains into it through the inlet on its side.
checks: The disposal unit: runs clear, no hum, no jam, no leak from the body, no reset needed
Splash guard and grind chamber: guard intact, no rust flaking off the ring
Mounting ring and sink flange: tight on the mount, no weep at the flange
P trap and slip joints: dry, no cracked slip washer
Drain and dishwasher line: high loop present, drains at full rate past the disposal
Switch and cord: no scorched cord ends, switch plate cool

toilet.what: A gravity toilet: tank and bowl. Seven checks and one standing offer; the running toilet is the most common found work in the trade.
toilet.how: The trip lever lifts the flapper, the tank dumps into the bowl, the siphon pulls the bowl down, and the fill valve refills the tank and the bowl. A flapper that stops sealing leaks silently all day; what you hear is the tank refilling at night.
checks: Flush handle: flushes on the first try, no wallow, chain not slack or broken
Inside the tank: flapper and seat clean, water level a half inch under the overflow tube
Flush valve: holds water, tank stays full with nothing running (dye test)
Fill valve: fills and shuts off clean, no hiss, no old ballcock
Supply line and angle stop: stop turns by hand, line dry, no crust
Tank to bowl bolts: tight, no seep
Base and wax seal: no rock, no stain at the base, floor solid, flange sound
Bidet seat: fitted and working, or offered

bath_vanity.what: The bathroom sink: stops, supplies, faucet, trap, pop up and the cabinet floor. Sixty seconds a sink and it finds work in most homes.
bath_vanity.how: Stops feed the faucet, the pop up lifts by its linkage, and waste goes down the tailpiece to the trap and into the wall. A trap that runs straight down with no vent is an S trap and it siphons dry.
checks: Angle stops, hot and cold: both turn and hold, no crust or seep
Supply lines: dry, no kinks, no corrosion, no cheap plastic nuts
Faucet and aerator: no drip at the base, full flow, aerator clear
P trap: dry joints, correct fall, no S trap
Pop up and drain: stopper seals and lifts, drains at full rate
Cabinet base: dry, no staining or swelling

shower.what: A single handle shower: cartridge, diverter, head, caulk, drain. The scaled head is a water quality conversation wearing a plumbing hat.
shower.how: One cartridge in the valve mixes hot and cold; the diverter sends the water up to the head instead of out the spout. Waste goes down the drain to the trap under the floor.
checks: Valve trim and cartridge: no drip after shutoff, temperature holds when a toilet flushes
Spout and diverter: diverter holds, no water splitting back out the spout
Showerhead: clear jets, full spray, no leak at the arm
Caulk and grout at wall and floor: continuous, no split, no missing grout
Drain and stopper: drains at full rate, no standing water

water_filter.what: A whole house water filter on the service line. Treatment where the water enters, so everything in the house gets filtered water instead of just one tap.
water_filter.how: All the house water passes through the tank's carbon media before the main. The valve head runs a backwash now and then to lift the media and send what it caught down the drain; the bypass valve takes it out of the line for service.
checks: Water quality (Every Plumbing): run the test kit, the numbers go on the sheet
Whole home filtration (Main shutoff card): fitted and in date, or not present
Bypass valve in service, not bypass
Backwash runs and the media is not spent

septic_lee.what: An aerobic treatment unit (Lee precast) with spray heads. Aeration is the whole point of the plant: no bubbles means nothing has been treated in a while, whatever the panel light says.
septic_lee.how: Sewage settles, the air pump at the house pushes air down the air line to the diffuser and bubbles it through the aeration chamber, the clarifier settles it again, the chlorinator tablets disinfect it, and the spray pump throws the treated water over the lawn through the heads. This plant has no panel: the air pump plugs into a GFCI receptacle and the pump and float splice in the riser.
checks: Tank lids: found, intact, sitting square, at grade
Lid security: bolted or screwed down, nothing a child could lift
Air compressor or aerator: running, warm, moving air
Aeration and dissolved oxygen: bubbling in the chamber, DO 2 or better
Compressor air filter: pulled, clean, refitted
Air diffusers: bubbling evenly, not just burping
Control panel: none on this plant, the pump is on a receptacle; alarm where fitted
Surge protection on the controls
Timer and dose settings: timed dosing only, rare
Chlorinator and tablets: charged with septic tablets, never pool tablets
Spray heads: all fire, rise and turn, aimed on the lawn, no standing water at the base
Pump vault and filter: screen clean, pump cycling right

septic_atu.what: An aerobic treatment unit with overland discharge (the AquaSafe here): an aerator, a clarifier and a chlorinator, no pump and no heads. Treated water leaves by gravity, so the aeration and the chlorinator are the system.
septic_atu.how: Air from the blower keeps the bacteria working in the aeration chamber, the clarifier settles the solids, the chlorinator disinfects the clear water, and it leaves by gravity to the discharge point. The panel at the house powers the blower and sounds the alarm if the air stops.
checks: Tank lids: found, intact, sitting square, at grade
Lid security: bolted or screwed down
Aeration and dissolved oxygen: bubbling in the chamber, DO 2 or better
Air compressor or aerator: running, warm, moving air
Compressor air filter: pulled, clean, refitted
Air diffusers: bubbling evenly
Control panel: no fault light, breaker on, alarm sounds on test, dry inside
Surge protection on the controls
Timer and dose settings: timed dosing only, rare
Chlorinator and tablets: charged with septic tablets, never pool tablets

septic_tank.what: A conventional septic tank feeding a drain field. Measure the sludge, do not eyeball it: the numbers are what make the pump out recommendation honest.
septic_tank.how: Solids settle in the tank and scum floats; the inlet tee drops the sewage under the scum, the outlet tee holds the scum back, and only the clear water in the middle leaves by gravity through the effluent filter to the field.
checks: Tank lids: found, intact, sitting square, at grade
Lid security: bolted or screwed down, nothing a child could lift
Scum and sludge levels: measured, both within normal
Inlet baffle or tee: in place, no roots, not channeling
Outlet baffle or tee: in place, not corroded off at the waterline
Water level: sitting at the outlet invert, not high, not low
Tank walls and seams: no crack, no groundwater coming in
Effluent filter: present and recently cleaned

septic_field.what: The drain field and its distribution box. The most expensive part of the system, and the one thing every protection item on the tank card is protecting.
septic_field.how: The D box splits the tank's outflow evenly into the field lines through its speed levelers, and the water soaks out of the gravel trenches into the soil. A box out of level sends everything down one trench and drowns it while the others stay dry.
checks: Ground surface: walked, no ponding, no soft spots
Odor: none over the field, even after rain
Vegetation: no lush green stripe over the lines
Traffic and cover: nothing parked or stored on it, no trees growing into it
D box: found and opened, lid off
D box sitting level, checked with a level
Outlets and speed levelers at the same height
No solids or standing effluent in the box
Box condition: no spalling, no roots, inlet sound

pump_tank.what: A pump tank: the second tank of a two tank spray system. Treated water collects here and the pump sends it out to the heads, on floats or on a timer.
pump_tank.how: Water from the plant collects in the tank. The float lifts and starts the pump through the plug in splices in the riser, the check valve holds the line when it stops, and the spray line carries the water to the heads. Most pump tanks are float controlled; a timer dosed one doses the field in measured drinks from the panel.
checks: Tank lids: found, intact, at grade
Lid security: bolted or screwed down
The pump: runs on a manual call, moves the level, amps in range
Floats and cords: free, set right, tested one at a time, cords sound at the entry
Liquid level against the floats: not above the alarm float, not drawn dry
Check valve and discharge: holds, no backflow, no leak at a joint
Control panel and breaker: dry, no fault light, breaker right
High level alarm: tested, audible and visible
Dose volume and cycle: what a dose measures here, against the design when you have it
How the pump is controlled: floats, or timer dosed from the panel
Pump vault and filter: screen clean, pump cycling right

pump_wiring.what: The plug in wiring for a spray pump: gray UF cable into the riser, splices to the pump and the float.
pump_wiring.how: Power comes in the UF cable through the cord grip, the float switch breaks the hot to the pump, the splices are crimped and heat shrunk, zip tied high in the riser out of the moisture.
checks: Splices dry, shrink intact
Zip tie at the lip, cords clear of the discharge
Float swings free
Cord grip tight
GFCI on the feed

lift_station.what: A lift station: a pump in a basin that pushes sewage up to the city sewer when gravity cannot. Test the alarm; an alarm nobody has ever heard is the same as no alarm at all.
lift_station.how: Sewage collects in the basin, the floats start and stop the pump, and it pushes up the force main through the check valve to the sewer. The panel on the wall runs it in Hand, Off or Auto and sounds the alarm when the water reaches the alarm float.
checks: The pump: runs on a manual call, moves the level, amps against the plate
Floats and cords: free, the sequence on, off, alarm proven, cords sound at the entry
Guide rails and lift chain: the pump can be pulled clean
Check valve and discharge: holds, basin does not refill from the line, no leak at a joint
Control panel and breaker: dry, sealed, no fault light, breaker right
High level alarm: tested for real
Basin, inlet and lid: no grease and rag mat, inlet clear, lid secured
Basin vent: to a real vent, never a drain, not buried

sump_pump.what: A sump pump in a basin under the hall bath, fed by the drain tile round the footing. Most of them discharge at the foundation, which means the same water walks straight back in.
sump_pump.how: Groundwater collects through the tile into the basin, the float lifts and starts the pump, the pump pushes it out the discharge through the check valve, and the panel on the girder feeds it and sounds the alarm when the water passes the alarm float.
checks: The pump: runs on a manual call, draws the basin down, does not run forever
Float and switch: travels free, not hung on a cord or the wall
Check valve: holds, the basin does not refill every cycle
Discharge line, and where it ends: well away from the foundation, not frozen or crushed
Basin, lid and inflow: no silt, a lid on it, not bone dry for years
Circuit and receptacle: its own circuit, no extension cord
Battery or water backup for a power cut

smart_shutoff_valve.what: An automatic (Flo) shutoff valve on the main: a motorized ball valve that senses a leak and shuts the water off by itself. A burst line runs until somebody comes home; this is the item that pays for itself the one time it works.
smart_shutoff_valve.how: It watches flow, pressure and temperature on the main and closes the valve on a leak, or from the app. The handle shows open or closed and turns by hand with the power out; the unions let it come out of the line without cutting pipe.
checks: Main shutoff: found, turns by hand, holds, a quarter turn ball valve not an old gate valve
Automatic leak shutoff valve: fitted and armed; this is it
Valve condition: no weeping at the stem after a turn
Does it actually stop the water: everything downstream goes quiet
Supply line off the valve sound at the unions
Label the main water shutoff so anybody can find it
Power and Wi Fi, the status light blue

flo_shutoff.what: An automatic (Flo) shutoff valve on the main: a motorized ball valve that senses a leak and shuts the water off by itself. A burst line runs until somebody comes home; this is the item that pays for itself the one time it works.
flo_shutoff.how: It watches flow, pressure and temperature on the main and closes the valve on a leak, or from the app. The handle shows open or closed and turns by hand with the power out; the unions let it come out of the line without cutting pipe.
checks: Main shutoff: found, turns by hand, holds, a quarter turn ball valve not an old gate valve
Automatic leak shutoff valve: fitted and armed; this is it
Valve condition: no weeping at the stem after a turn
Does it actually stop the water: everything downstream goes quiet
Supply line off the valve sound at the unions
Label the main water shutoff so anybody can find it
Power and Wi Fi, the status light blue

flo_shutoff_attic.what: An automatic (Flo) shutoff valve on the attic cold run, feeding the water heater. The same valve as the one on the main, where the attic heater's leak would start.
flo_shutoff_attic.how: It watches flow and pressure and closes on a leak. The brick plugs into the attic receptacle; the valve sits in the PEX run on its block.
checks: Valve type: a motorized quarter turn ball valve
Valve condition: no weeping at the unions or the PEX transitions
Does it actually stop the water: test close from the app or by hand
Reach and clearance: strapped on its block, reachable from the walkway
Supply line off the valve sound
Automatic leak shutoff: fitted and armed, power and Wi Fi

flo_shutoff_wall.what: An automatic (Flo) shutoff valve at the wall, on the house side of the main. The same valve as the one on the main, mounted where the service comes in.
flo_shutoff_wall.how: It watches flow and pressure and closes on a leak, or from the app. The handle turns by hand with the power out.
checks: Valve type: a motorized quarter turn ball valve
Valve condition: no weeping at the unions
Does it actually stop the water: test close
Reach and clearance: room to get at it
Supply line off the valve sound
Automatic leak shutoff: fitted and armed, power and Wi Fi

electric_panel.what: The load centre: the main breaker and the branch breakers.
electric_panel.how: The service feeds the main, the bus feeds each breaker, each breaker feeds a circuit. HVAC, water heater and septic have their own.
checks: Breaker sizes match the loads
No double taps
Dead front on
SPD status light
Torque and heat marks

whole_house_spd.what: A whole house surge protector in the panel. Protection at the equipment so a power blink does not take out a control board; out here the power flickers and the equipment does not get to shrug it off.
whole_house_spd.how: It sits across the bus on its own two pole breaker and clamps a surge to ground before it reaches the circuits. The green light says it still can; dark, it has done its job and is spent.
checks: Surge protection: present at the panel
They have one and it is not working right: status light dark
Short straight leads and its own breaker

outlet_surge.what: A surge receptacle at the treatment plant's air pump. Surge protection on the controls: one blink can take out the panel and stop the plant until somebody notices the smell.
outlet_surge.how: It clamps a surge on that circuit before it reaches the pump and the panel. The indicator light says it is still protecting.
checks: Surge protection on the controls: present
They have one and it is not working right: indicator light out
GFCI where required

hvac_surge.what: A surge protector at the condenser disconnect. Protection at the equipment so a power blink does not take out the control board, and a board is never the cheap day.
hvac_surge.how: It clamps a surge before the condenser's contactor and board. The indicator light says it is still protecting.
checks: Surge protection: present at the disconnect
They have one and it is not working right: indicator light out
Connections tight

easystart.what: A soft starter on the condenser. It lets the compressor ramp up instead of slamming on, so the lights do not dim and a generator can carry it.
easystart.how: It ramps the compressor up over a fraction of a second instead of letting it grab everything at once, cutting the start current by about two thirds. Wired in at the contactor and the run capacitor per its diagram.
checks: Compressor soft start: fitted
They have one and it is not working right: start current on a clamp, wiring per the diagram

sweet_air.what: A Sweet Air charcoal vent filter on the hall bath's vent stack where it comes through the roof. No deck card for this.
sweet_air.how: Sewer gas rises up the stack into the canister, passes through the activated carbon and leaves the slots clean. Twist the cap to OPEN and lift it off to change the carbon.
checks: Carbon fresh, not spent
Cap on, slots clear

water_softener.what: A water softener in the garage: hard water in, soft water out. Check bypass first, because half of them are sitting in bypass doing nothing at all.
water_softener.how: Water passes down through the resin bed and up the riser tube; the resin trades its sodium for the calcium and magnesium that scale up heaters and fixtures. When the meter says the bed is spent the valve head backwashes, draws brine from the salt tank through the resin to recharge it, rinses, and refills the brine tank, at night when nobody is drawing water.
checks: Softener unit: not in bypass, hardness test soft at the tap, resin still softening
Brine tank and salt: salt level good, no salt bridge (push a broom handle through)
Sediment prefilter: fitted and in date, pull it and show them
Drain and air gap: drain line to a legal point with an air gap, not kinked

pressure_tank.what: The well's pressure tank: a diaphragm tank with air on top and water below, so the pump is not always running. Pump and tank are one system; a waterlogged tank short cycles the pump until the pump is the problem.
pressure_tank.how: The pump fills the tank until the pressure switch opens at cut out (60 psi); the air charge pushes water out as taps run; at cut in (40 psi) the switch starts the pump again. The check valve holds the pressure when the pump stops.
checks: Pressure tank charge: holds air, not waterlogged, 2 psi under cut in with the tank empty
Pressure switch, cut in and cut out: at the right points, contacts clean
Pressure reading at the tank: steady through a full draw, builds and holds
Treatment ahead of the house: fitted and in date

well_pump.what: A submersible pump down a 6 inch cased well, pushing water up the drop pipe and out through the pitless adapter to the house. The cap on top is the lid on their drinking water.
well_pump.how: The pressure switch at the tank starts it. Water enters the intake screen, the stages push it up the drop pipe, the check valve above the pump holds the column when it stops, and the pitless adapter passes the line out through the casing below frost.
checks: Well cap and wiring: cap sealed and vermin proof, no wiring exposed at the cap
Casing 12 inches over grade, grade sloping away
The tank checks are on the pressure tank in the garage

condensate_pump.what: A small pump that lifts the condensing furnace's water to a drain when there is no gravity path from the closet. The A coil on top makes water all summer and it has to leave.
condensate_pump.how: Condensate runs from the furnace trap into the reservoir; the float lifts and runs the pump up the 3/8 inch tube to the drain. The safety switch opens the furnace's call for heat if the reservoir overfills.
checks: Condensate drain (A coil on top): trap primed, line pitched, no rust trail on the furnace
Reservoir clean, float free
Check valve and discharge tube not kinked, routed to a real drain
Safety switch wired to the furnace and tested
A test pour: it runs and stops

lift_station_duplex.what: A duplex grinder station: two grinder pumps on guide rails in one basin, pushing sewage up to the city sewer. Grinders die on rags and wipes; read the float stack from the top down and test the alarm.
lift_station_duplex.how: Four floats on a tree run it: STOP and LEAD start the lead pump, LAG brings the second pump on if the water keeps rising, ALARM lights the beacon. The panel swaps the lead pump every cycle so both wear evenly. Each pump lifts out on its chain, up its rail, with nothing to unbolt.
checks: The pump: each one in HAND runs, moves the level, amps against the plate
Floats and cords: free, the sequence stop, lead, lag, alarm proven
Cutter and impeller: not dulled or wound with wipes, passes solids
Guide rails and lift chain: each pump pulls clean and seats on its base elbow
Check valve and discharge: both hold, ball valves open
Small bore discharge: not restricted, a cleanout or flush point on the run
Control panel and breaker: dry, no fault light, fuses good, lead alternates
High level alarm: TEST button, beacon and horn
Basin, inlet and lid: no grease and rag mat, lid bolted, gasket good
Basin vent: clear, to a real vent

thermostat.what: The thermostat. It reads the room and tells the furnace, the air conditioner and the fan when to run. The one piece of the system the family touches every day.
thermostat.how: Five low voltage wires: R is 24 volt power, W calls heat, Y calls cool, G runs the fan, C is common. When the room drifts past the set point it closes the call and the equipment starts.
checks: The thermostat: what it is (smart, programmable, basic), display alive, batteries or C wire power, holds temperature
Heat, cool and fan each start on a call
Level and tight on the wall, sub base wires on the right terminals
Placement: not over a lamp, a register or in the sun
Smart thermostat upgrade: a schedule, phone control and visibility for us

shower_two.what: The tub and shower with two handles: a hot stem, a cold stem, a spout with a diverter, and the head. No anti scald protection on an old two handle valve; the scald risk is the one they have never been told about.
shower_two.how: Each handle opens its own stem valve and the two streams mix in the spout. Lifting the diverter on the spout sends the water up to the head. Waste goes down the drain shoe and the overflow to the trap under the tub.
checks: Hot stem: turns smooth, shuts off dry; a drip is the seat and washer
Cold stem: the same test, quoted with the hot while the wall is open
Anti scald protection: a mixing valve so a flush cannot send a scald to the shower
Tub spout diverter: stays up under load, no bleed to the spout
Showerhead: clear jets, full spray
Tub spout: no drip, no wobble, caulk line sound
Caulk and grout: continuous, no gaps at the tub or tile
Drain and stopper: drains at full rate
Bathtub card: access panel behind the tub wall
Bathtub card: overflow gasket, filled past the overflow and checked underneath
Bathtub card: stopper and trip lever hold water
Bathtub card: waste, shoe and trap under the tub, no weep
Bathtub card: tub surface and the floor at the apron

spray_pump_filter.what: The filter on the spray pump: a screen around the intake that keeps grit out of the pump and out of the spray heads. Skip it and you replace both.
spray_pump_filter.how: Water is drawn in through the screen; the heads downstream have small orifices, and a clogged head means the filter let something through or is torn.
checks: Pump vault and filter: screen clean, no tears, pump cycling right
Hosed off at every service
Pump seated back on its stand after cleaning

septic_aquaklear.what: An AquaKlear aerobic treatment unit: an aerator, a clarifier and a pump in a fiberglass tank. The deck's ATU cards do not say concrete or fiberglass, so the spray or overland card applies.
septic_aquaklear.how: Air from the blower keeps the bacteria working in the aeration chamber, the clarifier settles the solids and the airlift returns them, and the pump sends the clear water out to the spray heads through the chlorinator (or by gravity on the overland layout).
checks: Tank lids: found, intact, at grade
Lid security: bolted or screwed down
Air compressor or aerator: running, warm, moving air
Aeration and dissolved oxygen: bubbling, DO 2 or better
Compressor air filter: pulled, clean, refitted
Air diffusers: bubbling evenly
Control panel: no fault light, alarm sounds on test, dry inside
Surge protection on the controls
Chlorinator and tablets: charged with septic tablets
Spray heads and the pump vault filter on the spray layout

uni_lateral.what: A uni lateral check valve on the lift station force main: a check valve with a lever and weight, in its own box in the lawn.
uni_lateral.how: The flapper opens as the pump pushes water up and drops shut when it stops, so the force main does not drain back into the basin. The lever shows whether it is open or shut and lets you hold it open to drain the line.
checks: Check valve and discharge: holds, the basin does not refill from the force main after the pump stops
Lever moves freely
No weeping at the body or the unions

atu_blower_panel.what: The air pump for the treatment plant with its control panel, at the house wall (the AquaSafe overland plant).
atu_blower_panel.how: The panel powers the pump and watches it: a pressure or current alarm sounds if the air stops. The pump runs all the time and pushes air down the air line to the plant.
checks: Air compressor or aerator: running, warm, moving air, no loud bearing
Compressor air filter: pulled, clean, refitted
Control panel: no fault light, breaker on, alarm sounds on test, no water inside
Surge protection on the controls
Air line from the pump to the plant intact

atu_blower_outlet.what: The air pump for the treatment plant, plugged into a GFCI receptacle at the house wall with no panel.
atu_blower_outlet.how: The pump runs all the time on its own receptacle and pushes air down the air line to the plant. With no panel there is no alarm: a stopped pump shows up as a plant gone septic weeks later.
checks: Air compressor or aerator: running, warm, moving air, no loud bearing
Compressor air filter: pulled, clean, refitted
Control panel: none on this plant; the receptacle holds and its cover closes
Surge protection on the controls: a surge receptacle where fitted
Air line intact

spray_head_r22.what: A spray head on the treatment plant's spray line. It pops up under pressure and throws the treated water over the lawn; every one has to fire and land where it was designed to land.
spray_head_r22.how: The pump pressurizes the line, the head rises against its spring and the nozzle turns as it sprays. When the pump stops the head drops back flush with the grass.
checks: Spray heads: all fire, rise and turn when the pump runs
Spray pattern even, no clogged nozzle, on the lawn and off the house, the drive and the neighbour
No head cut off or removed, no standing water at the base
Drops back flush when the pump stops

spray_head_180_r22.what: A half circle spray head at the edge of the field. It throws a 180 degree pattern so the spray stays off the fence or the drive.
spray_head_180_r22.how: The pump pressurizes the line, the head rises against its spring and the nozzle turns as it sprays. When the pump stops the head drops back flush with the grass.
checks: Spray heads: all fire, rise and turn when the pump runs
Spray pattern even, no clogged nozzle, on the lawn and off the house, the drive and the neighbour
No head cut off or removed, no standing water at the base
Drops back flush when the pump stops

washer_box.what: The washer box: the recessed box in the laundry wall with the hot and cold valves and the standpipe. Rubber washer hoses are the number one homeowner flood in the country and the fix is under a hundred dollars.
washer_box.how: The hoses run from the valves to the washer. The washer pumps its water up into the standpipe, which drains down through a trap. The valves are the shutoffs when the washer is not in use; hammer arrestors on them take the bang when the washer snaps its water off.
checks: Washer hoses: braided steel, no bulge at the couplings, rubber ones replaced
Shutoff valves: turn and hold, a single lever box they will actually use
Water hammer arrestors on both lines, no bang when the washer shuts off
Standpipe and trap: right height, trapped, no overflow on the spin cycle
Pan and drain under an upstairs laundry

attic_ladder.what: The pull down attic ladder in the garage ceiling.
attic_ladder.how: The door swings down on springs and the ladder unfolds. It is the way up to the attic equipment.
checks: Springs and hinges tight
Ladder feet sit flat
Door closes and seals

trash_tank.what: A trash tank: a small septic tank in front of the aerobic plant, the first tank the house sewer reaches. Everything the plant should never have to chew on stops here.
trash_tank.how: Solids settle to the floor, grease and paper float, and only the clear middle leaves through the outlet tee to the plant, so the plant treats liquid and not trash. Read the sludge like any tank; it protects the aeration chamber.
checks: Tank lids: found, intact, at grade
Lid security: bolted down
Scum and sludge levels: measured, both within normal
Inlet baffle or tee: in place, no roots
Outlet baffle or tee: in place, not corroded off
Water level: at the outlet invert
Tank walls and seams: no crack, no groundwater

wh_surge_protector.what: A surge protective device on the water heater's own circuit. Protection at the equipment so a power blink does not take out the thermostats and elements.
wh_surge_protector.how: It sits across the two hots and ground. When the voltage spikes it turns into a short for a split second and sends the surge to ground instead of through the heater's controls. The green light says it still can.
checks: Surge protection on the water heater: present
They have one and it is not working right: status light dark, soot at the nipple, a cracked housing
How it is wired: across both hots and ground in the heater's junction box

thermostatic_mixing_valve.what: A thermostatic mixing valve on the water heater's hot outlet. The tank can be kept hot so you never run out while the valve tempers the water down to around 120 before it reaches the taps, so nobody gets scalded.
thermostatic_mixing_valve.how: Hot from the tank and cold from the supply meet in the valve. A wax element slides a shuttle between the two seats so the water leaving is held at the set temperature, even with the tank turned up. Unions let it come out without cutting pipe.
checks: Thermostatic mixing valve on the hot outlet: present and holding temper at the tap
Temperature setting: 120 at the tap, the tank can run hotter
Anti scald protection: a toilet flush cannot send a scald to the shower
Piping at the valve: H the hot inlet, C the cold inlet, M the mixed outlet, the cold check in

thermostatic_mixing_valve_pex.what: A thermostatic mixing valve on the water heater's hot outlet, piped in PEX. The same anti scald protection, fed through an 18 inch stainless connector off the tank.
thermostatic_mixing_valve_pex.how: Same valve: hot and cold meet, the wax element holds the mixed temperature. On PEX it is fed through the connector off the tank (no PEX in the first 18 inches off a water heater), with crimp fittings and copper rings on every joint.
checks: Thermostatic mixing valve on the hot outlet: present and holding temper at the tap
Temperature setting: 120 at the tap, the tank can run hotter
Anti scald protection: a toilet flush cannot send a scald to the shower
Piping at the valve: H the hot inlet, C the cold inlet, M the mixed outlet, the cold check in
Crimp joints: the ring 3/16 inch back from the tube end, crimped square

air_quality_monitor.what: An indoor air quality monitor on the hall wall. A sensor that shows what the indoor air is actually doing, so air quality is a number on their phone instead of an argument.
air_quality_monitor.how: It draws room air through its sensors and reads particles (PM2.5), CO2, chemicals (VOCs), temperature and humidity, and scores the air. It is how the homeowner sees what a filter, a purifier or fresh air is doing.
checks: Air quality monitor: present and reporting
They have one and it is not working right: dark display, adapter unplugged, no Wi Fi
Placement: clear of the slots on both sides, away from the kitchen

media_air_cleaner.what: A media air cleaner cabinet under the furnace: a deep pleated filter, four to five inches instead of one. The single biggest air quality upgrade for the least money, changed once a year instead of monthly.
media_air_cleaner.how: All the return air passes through the deep pleated media before the blower. It catches far more than a 1 inch filter without choking the system; the old filter slot is blocked off.
checks: Deep pleat media cabinet: present and in service
Current filter: the right type and size, no air bypassing the frame
They have one and it is not working right: media loaded grey and caked, past due

induct_purifier.what: An in duct air purifier on the supply plenum. Carbon or PCO purification goes after what a filter cannot: odors, gases and biological growth in the system itself.
induct_purifier.how: A UV lamp in a catalytic cell makes oxidizers and ions that ride out with the supply air to treat odors, germs and particles. It runs off 24 volts from the furnace; the lamp window glows when it is on.
checks: Carbon or PCO purifier: present and in service
They have one and it is not working right: lamp dark, cell spent (about every 2 years)

hosebib_protection.what: The hose bib with its freeze cover and vacuum breaker. No vacuum breaker means a hose left in a bucket can pull that water back into what the family drinks.
hosebib_protection.how: The foam cover holds the house's warmth around the bib in a freeze. The vacuum breaker on the hose thread opens its vent and breaks the siphon when the pressure drops, so dirty hose water cannot be pulled back into the house.
checks: The spigot itself: turns, shuts off dry, no drip at the packing, not loose in the wall
Vacuum breaker fitted on every hose bib
Static pressure reading: gauge on the bib, everything off, 50 to 70 is healthy
Freeze cover on for winter, hose off (not a deck check yet)

erv.what: An energy recovery ventilator in the attic. A tight modern house holds onto its own air; this brings in a controlled amount of fresh air without losing the comfort.
erv.how: Stale air leaves from the kitchen and fresh air comes in through the roof. The two streams pass each other in the core and trade heat and moisture without mixing. The interlock brings the air handler blower on whenever it runs.
checks: Fresh air ventilator: present and in service
They have one and it is not working right: core packed, filters loaded, caps blocked, control dark
Outside caps clear, intake below and away from the exhaust
Ducts and the wall control

sludgehammer.what: A SludgeHammer aerobic bacteria generator in the septic tank. It keeps feeding the system live culture: a field that keeps digesting is a field that does not get replaced.
sludgehammer.how: An air pump by the tank bubbles air up through the media in the column, growing aerobic bacteria that eat sludge and scum and clean the effluent before it reaches the field. The blend bag on its stick feeds the culture.
checks: Aerobic bacteria generator: present and running
They have one and it is not working right: no bubble plume, air pump off, alarm lit
Blend bag fresh
Sludge and scum still in range

grease_interceptor.what: A 1,000 gallon two compartment precast concrete grease interceptor behind a restaurant. Measure the grease cap and the solids against the liquid depth; this is a measurement, not a glance, same as a septic tank.
grease_interceptor.how: Kitchen water slows down in the first compartment: grease floats to the top, solids sink. The clear middle crosses the baffle and leaves through the outlet tee to the city sewer. It gets pumped out on a schedule and the log stays on site.
checks: Trap type and where it sits: sized for the kitchen, in the ground, not an under sink trap doing an in ground job
Lid and access: gasketed, a traffic rated cover where anything drives
Grease and solids depth: measured with a stick against the liquid depth
Baffles and tees: in place, not broken or corroded off
Inlet and outlet lines: inlet not greased over, outlet not carrying grease toward the main
Pump out record on site

commercial_storefront.what: The restaurant the grease interceptor serves.
commercial_storefront.how: The kitchen's sinks, floor sinks and dishwasher drain to the interceptor out back; the restroom goes straight to the sewer.
checks: What goes through the interceptor
At the building exit

dishwasher_line.what: The dishwasher connection: the supply line and its stop, the drain hose with its high loop or air gap, and the floor in front of the machine. We do not fix the machine; the lines are ours.
dishwasher_line.how: The hot line runs from its own stop under the sink to the machine. The drain hose rises in a high loop above the connection, or through an air gap on the deck, before it drops into the disposal or the tailpiece, so sink water cannot siphon back into the dishes.
checks: Supply line and shutoff: its own stop, turns by hand, no kink behind the machine
Drain hose, high loop or air gap: present, no backflow
Under the door and the floor in front: no leak at the door, no swollen flooring
Water quality at the machine: spotting and film on the glassware is the water, not the detergent
